api.title: The whole surface
api.lead: There is not much of it, and that is the point. Five things to know.

foot.note: MIT · built by alban.pasquelin · the chassis on this page is the library itself

cards.what0: The smallest chassis that works. Two columns, a band, a centre — and a header of your own driving it.
cards.tip0: Panels sharing a zone and a slot take turns; the rail switches between them. Give a panel the secondary slot to stack it under the first instead.
cards.what1: The centre is an outlet. Navigating changes the middle and nothing else — columns keep their width, open panels stay open.
cards.tip1: Declare the panels in the layout route, above the outlet. Declared per page, they would unmount on every navigation and lose whatever they held.
cards.what2: The centre carries documents on Dockview — draggable, splittable tabs — while panels stay on the edges.
cards.tip2: Import it from the dockview entry point so its weight only lands on the projects that want tabs. Tool panels never enter the centre: a document has a name, a panel has an icon.
cards.what3: The same chassis under four palettes. Colours, radius, rail width, header height — all custom properties.
cards.tip3: Set the accent token on any ancestor and the chassis inherits your brand instead of imposing one. Need to go further? Every piece is exported and replaceable on its own.

api5.body0: A panel is a descriptor. Where it hangs, what it is called, what it draws.
api5.body1: One hook for every header, shortcut or menu that needs to act on the panels.
api5.body2: Build the store yourself and a socket, a native menu or a worker can open a panel.
api5.body3: Every value is a custom property. Set the accent and the rails follow your brand.
api5.body4: The components are built on hooks that render nothing. Draw your own frame on them.
